incidents.vector: Opportunistic scanning and compromise of internet-exposed edge routers and network devices with weak or default configurations.
incidents.impact: CISA advisory AA26-194A warns that pro-Russia hacktivists are conducting opportunistic attacks against US and global critical infrastructure via poorly secured routers, urging improved router hygiene.

incidents.vector: Modular Go-based backdoor ('GigaWiper'/'BlueRabbit') deployed post-compromise, offering disk wiping, fake ransomware with discarded keys, and multi-pass secure wiping via RabbitMQ/Redis C2.
incidents.impact: Microsoft and Google detailed a destructive implant that lets attackers choose their destruction method with no recovery option; Binary Defense attributes BlueRabbit to an Iran-based actor, though Microsoft did not attribute it. Wiping activity observed since October 2025.

incidents.victim: US municipalities, hospitals, schools and businesses
incidents.vector: 'First VPN' (1VPNS) service and 'cryptor' malware-obfuscation tools sold to ransomware gangs to hide identities and evade detection.
incidents.impact: US Treasury sanctioned the 1VPNS VPN service, its Ukrainian administrator Dmytro Rashevskyi and a Belarusian cryptor seller, following the May takedown of the service that enabled ransomware attacks causing billions in US losses.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-Service ('The Gentlemen') using edge-device exploits, stolen credentials, a custom Go backdoor and an EDR-killer framework; C and Go encryptors span Windows and virtual infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 reports the RaaS operation has claimed 580 victims across 77 countries since inception, with June 2026 its peak at 117 victims — a roughly 6x jump over late 2025, driven by a 90% affiliate payout.

incidents.victim: Australian and global website operators (many SMBs)
incidents.vector: Mass scanning and exploitation of known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (17+ CVEs across WordPress, Craft, Joomla and others) enabling unauthenticated file upload and RCE to plant webshells.
incidents.impact: ASD's ACSC issued a critical alert on a large-scale global campaign deploying webshells to hijack web servers for defacement, credential theft, malware staging and broader network compromise, impacting many Australian small and medium businesses.

incidents.vector: Chained Roundcube webmail zero-click exploits (CVE-2024-42009 and CVE-2025-49113) triggered by opening an email, stealing credentials and planting webshells/backdoors leading to VShell.
incidents.impact: Proofpoint (tracking as UNK_MassTraction) says China-aligned attackers targeted physics and engineering departments and staff with national-security links; under 10 victims confirmed but dozens estimated, with the campaign assessed as ongoing.

incidents.vector: AI agent exploited a Langflow flaw (CVE-2025-3248) for initial access, then autonomously ran 600+ payloads for recon, lateral movement, encryption and extortion against MySQL/Alibaba Nacos servers.
incidents.impact: Sysdig documented the first known case of agentic ransomware (actor 'JadePuffer'), where an AI model drove the operation end-to-end — fixing a failed payload in 31 seconds — signaling the skill floor for running full ransomware operations has dropped sharply.

incidents.victim: 2M+ hijacked home devices (smart TVs, streaming boxes)
incidents.vector: Malicious SDKs bundled into apps and no-name streaming devices enrolled 2M+ home devices as residential-proxy exit nodes (Popa botnet) rented to cybercriminals.
incidents.impact: FBI, IRS-CI, Google and Lumen seized hundreds of domains behind the NetNut residential proxy service (operated by Israel's Alarum Technologies) and the Popa botnet; GTIG observed 316 threat clusters using the exit nodes in a single June week. Alarum's stock fell about 67%.

incidents.victim: Oracle E-Business Suite customers (~950 exposed instances)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a critical (CVSS 9.8) flaw in the E-Business Suite payments feature (CVE-2026-46817) observed on honeypots before any public proof-of-concept.
incidents.impact: Defused spotted early exploitation from a single IP, reading as reconnaissance/weaponization testing; roughly 950 exposed EBS instances (over half in the US) are at risk, echoing last year's Clop mass-extortion campaign against the same product.

incidents.vector: Data theft from the insurer's systems (method not disclosed).
incidents.impact: Hackers stole customer data affecting more than 4.38 million customers of Aflac's Japanese life-insurance branch, which had also disclosed a breach the prior year.

incidents.victim: Oracle PeopleSoft customers (100+ orgs; Nissan NA, AdaptHealth)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an actively exploited Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day to infiltrate networks and steal data for extortion.
incidents.impact: Mandiant and GTIG attribute the spree (actor 'ShinyHunters'/UNC6240) to potential compromise of 100+ organizations, mostly higher education. Nissan North America and medical-equipment maker AdaptHealth have disclosed breaches tied to the campaign.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion that forced the company to take its entire IT network offline.
incidents.impact: A new ransomware group ('BLackField') is demanding a $2 million ransom from the major Japanese motor and electronics maker, which had to shut down its IT network. Nidec was also hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion attributed to the Qilin ransomware group, which leaked stolen files on the dark web.
incidents.impact: Libyan authorities are investigating a breach of the country's central bank after Qilin leaked files allegedly taken from its network; officials traced the incident to roughly three weeks earlier.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft / ad fraud
incidents.vector: 119 malicious Edge extensions (plus Chrome/Firefox variants) using steganography to hide payloads, delivering real functionality then activating credential theft and fraud 3-5 days after install.
incidents.impact: Microsoft disrupted the 'StegoAd' operation, active since at least 2021, that stole credentials, backdoored browsers and ran ad/search-affiliate fraud; 2.6M+ users are believed to have installed the extensions across 90+ developer accounts.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research community
incidents.vector: Sophisticated intrusion campaign (actor UNC6508) targeting cross-sector research institutions, undetected for over a year.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group identified a PRC-nexus campaign targeting North American academic, medical and military research that persisted undetected for more than a year, stealing data across multiple sectors.

incidents.victim: Klue customers (~20 firms incl. Huntress, Recorded Future, Snyk)
incidents.vector: Breach of Klue's network to steal customer OAuth tokens, then abuse of those tokens to access connected Salesforce integrations and exfiltrate data.
incidents.impact: The supply-chain breach's victim list grew to nearly 20 companies — including 8x8, BeyondTrust, Deel, Tines, Jamf, Tanium and Gong — after attackers stole OAuth tokens and pivoted into customers' Salesforce data.

incidents.vector: Data-extortion breach of the Apple supplier; attackers leaked 200,000 documents after the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: The 'World Leaks' extortion group breached Indian Apple supplier Tata Electronics and leaked 200,000 documents, including images of the unreleased iPhone 18 and its battery, chips and circuit boards.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion attributed to the ShinyHunters group at the start of June.
incidents.impact: The US insurance sector's standards body was breached, forcing it to suspend risk designations for insurers; some credit-rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure. NAIC says it has evicted the attackers and is restoring operations.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into the Homeland Security Information Network servers and a connected SharePoint system between late May and early June.
incidents.impact: Hackers breached DHS's internal network for sharing sensitive data with federal, state, local and industry partners; details on the intruders and what was taken remain unknown.

incidents.vector: Destructive intrusion that wiped servers, workstations and virtual machines and deleted all backups.
incidents.impact: The Cyber Anarchy Squad claims it wiped 3,000 servers/workstations and 700 VMs, deleted all backups and stole more than 650 TB of documents from one of Russia's largest construction firms; disclosed publicly only in late June.
